answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may bid for work. A verifier assigns jobs unpredictably and checks sampled outputs; a proven duplicate or coordinated fraud burns the stake and can exclude linked accounts. This does not make Sybils impossible: an attacker can still create many keys, but must fund each one and risks losing that capital. A plume of cheap identities cannot cheaply fake a pearl of trustworthy history, while umber marks on the ledger make forfeitures visible.
